bugs.title: Configuration surface is entirely non-functional: settings.json is never read (master `enabled` switch + all knobs ignored)
bugs.description:
The entire configuration surface documented in the PRD (§7 Configuration surface, §09-configuration.md) and the README (§3 Configuration + the "Disabling" subsection) is not implemented. The extension factory hard-codes `setConfig(undefined)` at src/index.ts:30 and the code comment explicitly admits it: "v1: validated defaults — no Pi settings accessor in v1; setConfig(undefined) → DEFAULT_CONFIG; reading real settings.mulligan is v1.1". No code anywhere reads Pi's settings.json. I verified against the installed Pi 0.84.1 type definitions that neither ExtensionAPI nor ExtensionContext exposes a settings accessor, and `rg setConfig` shows `src/index.ts:30` is the only call site — it always passes undefined. `config.ts validateConfig()` is fully capable of validating a raw settings object (and is unit-tested), but it is never fed real user settings.

Concrete user-facing impact (contradicts documented behavior):
- README.md:103-109 promises: "`enabled: false` makes the ENTIRE extension a no-op … The human can disable Mulligan without uninstalling it." This is FALSE. Setting `"mulligan": { "enabled": false }` in `~/.pi/agent/settings.json` or `.pi/settings.json` has ZERO effect — the `context` filter still transforms messages, the bloat/drift/high-water nudges still fire, and the tools do NOT refuse with "Mulligan is disabled". `contextHandler` / `bloatReminderHandler` / `turnEndMetricHandler` all call `getConfig()` which returns DEFAULT_CONFIG (enabled:true) regardless of user settings.
- Every other documented knob is likewise ignored: `nudges.bloatThresholdBytes`, `nudges.bloatReminder`, `nudges.perTurnDrift`, `rewind.maxRetriesPerPrompt`, `rewind.abortContextFraction`, `rewind.maxDepth`, `audit.estimateConfidence`, and crucially `log.file` (the primary observability/debugging surface per spec §10) can NEVER be enabled by a user.
- This also undermines the E22 runaway-loop backstops' customizability — a user who needs to tune `maxRetriesPerPrompt`/`abortContextFraction` for their workflow cannot.

This violates PRD §7 ("Mulligan reads `mulligan` from Pi settings.json"), spec/09 §1 ("Mulligan reads a `mulligan` object from Pi's settings.json … loaded lazily … re-read on /reload"), spec/03 design principle (works with zero config BUT honors config when present), and the README's prominent Configuration + Disabling documentation. It is a wholesale missing feature masquerading as implemented (the README actively documents a non-existent capability, including a safety off-switch). Borderline-critical: the advertised master disable switch silently does nothing.
bugs.reproduction:
1. Add `{ "mulligan": { "enabled": false } }` to `~/.pi/agent/settings.json` (or project-local `.pi/settings.json`).
2. Run `pi -e ./src/index.ts -p "hello"` (or load in TUI).
3. Observe: Mulligan is NOT disabled. The drift/bloat nudges still fire; if you trigger a rewind, the tool does NOT refuse "Mulligan is disabled".
4. Equivalently, set any knob (e.g. `nudges.bloatThresholdBytes: 1` to force every result to be flagged) — it has no effect.
Root cause: src/index.ts:30 `setConfig(undefined);` is the only config initialization; validateConfig(undefined) always yields DEFAULT_CONFIG. Fix: the factory/session_start must obtain the merged Pi settings and call `setConfig(settings.mulligan)` (note: Pi's ExtensionAPI exposes no settings accessor in 0.84.1, so a real fix must find the settings path or add an accessor — until then the README/spec must not advertise config as working).

bugs.title: Project fails strict TypeScript type-check (tsc --noEmit): stale SessionRuntime test fixture
bugs.description: `npx tsc --noEmit` (using the project's tsconfig.json which `include`s both `src` and `test`) exits non-zero with one TS2352 error. In test/drift_nudge.test.ts:239 a hand-built `SessionRuntime` fixture omits the `rewindRefusedTurnIndex` field that was added to the `SessionRuntime` type by the later P4 drift-nudge-mute work (src/runtime.ts / consumed by src/filter.ts and src/tools/rewind.ts). The cast `as SessionRuntime` therefore fails strict type-checking. The runtime behavior is unaffected (the missing field reads as `undefined` and vitest transpiles without type-checking, so all 882 tests pass), but the project does not type-check cleanly — a standard CI `tsc --noEmit` gate would fail, and the fixture is stale relative to the type.
bugs.reproduction:
Run `npx tsc --noEmit` in the repo root. Output (single error):
  test/drift_nudge.test.ts(239,10): error TS2352: Conversion of type '{ sessionId: string; seq: number; tokenBaseline: null; lastTurnIndex: null; lastFiltered: null; lastFilterTs: null; pendingBloatHits: never[]; shrinkMissCounts: Map<any,any>; aboveHighWater: boolean; }' to type 'SessionRuntime' may be a mistake ... Property 'rewindRefusedTurnIndex' is missing ...
Fix: add `rewindRefusedTurnIndex: null` (or cast through `unknown`) to the fixture object.

summary:
End-to-end validation of pi-mulligan against its PRD. I read every core module (index, config, transforms, filter, nudges, notes, markers, ledger, tokens, runtime, and all five tools), cross-referenced the PRD/README/spec against the implementation, verified against the installed Pi 0.84.1 .d.ts types, ran the full unit suite (882/882 passing), and ran the real integration smoke harness against pi 0.84.1 + glm-5.2 (14/14 scenarios passing: F-rewind-core, F-shrink-persist, F-shrink-preventive, F-nudge-drift, F-protected, F-maxdepth, F-checkpoint, F-failopen, F-reload, E7, E11, E12, E15, E20). I also observed the extension's nudges operating live on my own session (bloat reminders on large reads; drift nudges on sustained growth) — the windowed drift logic, rendering, pairing-aware transforms, pinned-hide permanence (BUG-001/002 regression guards), cancel/marker-retraction, D5 filtered-view audit, soft-delete (no disk mutation), zero-extra-request nudges, and fail-open discipline are all correct and spec-compliant.

The one substantial defect is a wholesale missing feature: the documented settings.json configuration surface is never read (index.ts calls setConfig(undefined)), so the master `enabled:false` off-switch and every other knob silently do nothing — directly contradicting PRD §7, spec §09, and the README's Configuration/Disabling sections. A second, minor defect is that the project does not pass `tsc --noEmit` (one stale test fixture). Core rewind/shrink/checkpoint/audit/cancel functionality and the E22 runaway-loop backstops work correctly out of the box via defaults; the gap is configurability/disability.
recommendations: Wire the extension to actually read Pi's merged settings and call setConfig(settings.mulligan) — at minimum in the factory and on session_start/reload. Since Pi 0.84.1's ExtensionAPI/ExtensionContext expose no settings accessor, this likely requires either adding an accessor upstream or reading the settings file directly; until it exists, correct the README/spec to stop advertising config (especially the `enabled:false` disable switch) as a working capability.
Fix the stale SessionRuntime fixture in test/drift_nudge.test.ts:239 (add rewindRefusedTurnIndex) and add a CI `tsc --noEmit` gate so the project type-checks cleanly.

Consider integration-testing the §5.2 high-water nudge and the E22 context-fraction guard (currently only unit-tested); note the abortContextFraction guard uses the last context-fire's filtered view (excludes the current turn's just-produced tool results), so it lags one turn in the exact re-bloat loop it targets — acceptable and spec-consistent, but worth a comment/test.
